stories.headline: Russia signals readiness for new US-Ukraine talks after Kyiv missile strike

sources.body: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and forcing residents into shelters, Ukrainian authorities said Thursday, hours after Moscow signalled readiness to resume US-mediated peace talks. President Donald Trump said negotiations were closer than ever to ending the war, though the Kremlin expressed doubts over Ukrainian and European proposals.
sources.headline: Russian missiles hit Kyiv as Moscow signals readiness for peace talks

sources.body: Moscow is ready to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks next month, the Kremlin said Wednesday after President Vladimir Putin met with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Russia. FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg has more.
sources.headline: Kremlin says 'ready' to resume 3-way talks with US and Ukraine mid-November

stories.headline: Houthi attacks prompt US diplomatic departures from Saudi Arabia

sources.body:
Reports emerge of similar withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns about a return to conflict with Iran after US midterm elections

The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia , as the gulf kingdom faces a barrage of near-daily attacks, with at least three people killed at an airport and oilfield on Wednesday evening.

Attacks on “civilian airports and other critical infrastructure” by the Iranian-supported Houthis in Yemen were highlighted as the reason for the drawdown. State department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said: “The safety and security of department personnel and their families remain our highest priority.”

The state department said the order covered its embassy in Riyadh and its satellite consulates. The embassy had been badly damaged at the start of the US war on Iran and had been operating with only a skeleton staff for months, although in recent weeks some diplomats had returned.

The announcement comes as some media – including NBC and AFP – reported that families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn from the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, while the New York Times said the Trump administration was developing plans to restart the war on Iran.

However in his statement on Wednesday, Pigott described the reports of further withdrawals as “inaccurate” and stressed that the state department order was for the departure of staff and their families from Saudi Arabia only.

Saudi Arabia has faced a succession of deadly attacks from the Houthis over recent weeks, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.

On Thursday the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority announced that two people were killed in overnight attacks on King Fahad international airport in Dammam, on the Gulf near Bahrain and Qatar.

Eight people were injured and the airport also suffered some material damage, according to officials. Global flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said flights had been diverted away from the airport.

Separately, falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility in the country’s south-east also killed two people and injured a further two, the Saudi energy ministry said.

Neither attack was immediately claimed by the Houthis, but airports and oil facilities have been a major target of the militant group in their recent wave of missile and projectile strikes on Saudi Arabia.

The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February. NBC reported that the US military has been quietly scaling back its presence at bases across the Middle East in recent days, however a spokesperson from US central command told the US outlet that service members are regularly moved to “optimize mission readiness”.

The withdrawal of staff from the region comes amid reports that Trump has been presented with plans for restarting strikes on Iran, after the midterm elections.
sources.headline: Some US diplomats told to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks

sources.body:
All injured individuals were immediately transported to hospitals, civil aviation says updates to come.

One person has been killed and eight injured in an attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd International Airport in the eastern city of Dammam, the country’s civil aviation authority announced.

All of the wounded, whose injuries range from minor to critical, were transported to hospitals to receive medical attention, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said in a statement on Wednesday.

Earlier in the day, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oilfield, the Ministry of Energy said.

It was the latest in a series of assaults on Saudi airports as conflict intensifies between Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Last week, the kingdom reported that a projectile strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 11 killed one person and injured 11. On October 10, the civil aviation authority reported that a separate attack on the same airport claimed the lives of 12 people and injured more than 300.

On Wednesday, the US State Department ordered diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia amid the ongoing Houthi attacks. There are also plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.

The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia.
sources.headline: One killed, eight injured in attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Fahd airport

stories.headline: France bans protests after violent unrest as Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploitation

sources.body: French police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as authorities braced for further demonstrations following some of the worst street unrest in years. The restrictions came after President Emmanuel Macron appeared to accuse US President Donald Trump of exploiting the violence for political gain ahead of US midterm elections. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
sources.headline: Live: Paris bans protests after violent unrest as Macron takes swipe at Trump

sources.body:
Leaders criticised for spreading misleading information as France prepares for further protests this weekend

Emmanuel Macron has accused Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of making “stupid comments” about France’s street unrest for political gain, as the country prepared for more protests this weekend.

Speaking during a visit to Qatar, the French president did not name names but said “manipulation of information” after Saturday’s riots had led to “comments that are as unacceptable as they are stupid, from many people, including foreign leaders”.

Asked if he was referring to Donald Trump, Macron replied: “Among others.” The US president has blamed France’s violence on “migrants, jihadists and communists” as he campaigns for his Republican party before midterm elections.

Macron told reporters in Doha that some leaders “in the middle of election campaigns, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic” were “naively spreading narratives that certain circles are clearly trying to promote”.

They were “using our country for their own political campaigns”, the French president said. “And we don’t need that. We already have difficulties to deal with.”

He said AI-generated images were circulating “depicting scenes that never actually happened in France . We’ve had people claiming that we were invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false.”

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces elections next weekend, has also said that France had been hit by an “invasion of extremist Islam”. Analysts have dismissed claims that migrants were the main factor in France’s protests.

Macron and his government are struggling to get on top of a crisis that has erupted six months before presidential elections to choose his successor. The government has admitted it “lost control” over widespread rioting on Saturday.

Largely peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living rapidly descended into rampant violence and extensive looting , especially in Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Limoges, where the town hall was set on fire and partly destroyed.

Police said that protests would be banned in parts of Paris on Thursday as the city braced for more demonstrations.

The ban, from 8am to 8pm, will apply to key landmarks, including the Elysee presidential palace, both houses of parliament, and tourist havens such as the Louvre museum and the Champs-Elysees.

Other areas where rallies will be prohibited include the Bastille and République squares, and the Châtelet-Les Halles shopping area which was heavily targeted by looters over the weekend.

The unrest has prompted several countries to issue travel warnings for France and rattled already nervous financial markets, with the yield on the French government’s benchmark 10-year bonds passing 5% on Wednesday , its highest since 2002.

Macron pledged to prevent any repeat of last weekend’s convulsions, as the gilets jaunes (yellow vest) grassroots protest movement formally filed plans for a march through the centre of Paris ⁠on Saturday that is likely to be the ⁠government’s next big test.
sources.headline: Macron accuses Trump and other foreign leaders of ‘stupid comments’ about France unrest

stories.headline: UN warns the world is on course to breach the 1.5°C warming limit

sources.body: The UN is warning that global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals of 1.5 degrees Celsius warming – and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century. The report by the United Nations Environment Programme lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November's COP31 climate summit - set to take place next month in Turkey. Story by Emerald Maxwell.
sources.headline: World set to breach 1.5°C warming limit set by Paris Climate Agreement

stories.headline: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica-related claims

sources.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. Meta called the penalty “a tax on speech".
sources.headline: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal

sources.body:
Mark Zuckerberg, director ejecutivo de Meta, empresa que aglutina Facebook entre otras, prueba sus gafas inteligentes mientras cada vez está más bajo sospecha por cómo dirige su negocio 

Meta fue condenada el miércoles por un juez Nuevo México a pagar 25.000 millones de dólares por engañar a los usuarios sobre sus prácticas de privacidad de datos, una de las mayores multas impuestas contra un gigante tecnológico. El caso deriva del asunto de Cambridge Analytica, que estalló hace casi una década, tras las elecciones que llevaron a Donald Trump a la Casa Blanca por primera vez.

En 2021, Nuevo México demandó a Meta, la empresa de Mark Zuckerberg, la matriz de Facebook, por un escándalo relacionado con esa consultora política que contrató la campaña de Trump, alegando que la empresa de redes sociales había engañado a los usuarios con sus declaraciones públicas sobre su política de privacidad.

La sanción se produce después de que un jurado de un tribunal de Santa Fe declarara en septiembre responsable al gigante tecnológico de haber engañado a los ciudadanos del estado sobre cómo protege y recopila los datos de los usuarios y sobre las medidas que adopta para impedir la proliferación de contenidos perjudiciales en sus servicios.

“El extraordinario número de infracciones deliberadas constatadas por el jurado, la duración y reiteración de la conducta, la amplitud de los asuntos en los que se produjeron las infracciones, la implicación de altos cargos de Facebook, el tamaño de la audiencia alcanzada en Nuevo México y el carácter claramente intencionado y sistemático de las repetidas declaraciones falsas de Facebook, acreditado durante el juicio, justifican la aplicación de la sanción máxima permitida por la Ley de Nuevo México contra las prácticas desleales: 5.000 dólares por cada infracción constatada por el jurado”, escribió el juez Francis Mathew.

El magistrado añadió que la sanción devengará intereses al tipo del 15% anual hasta que se abone íntegramente.

Meta ya había resuelto diversas demandas por vulneración de la privacidad derivadas del caso Cambridge Analytica en distintos puntos de EE.UU. como parte de un acuerdo global alcanzado en agosto por casi 17.000 millones de dólares con una coalición de fiscales generales estatales, en otro procedimiento federal relacionado con la seguridad infantil y la salud mental.

Sin embargo, como Nuevo México no formaba parte de ese acuerdo, el caso estatal sobre privacidad de datos relacionado con el escándalo de Cambridge Analytica siguió adelante y llegó a juicio en septiembre.

En 2022, la empresa matriz de Facebook aceptó pagar 725 millones de dólares para resolver una demanda colectiva que también surgió del escándalo de Cambridge Analytica. El caso sacudió a la compañía dirigida de Zuckerberg antes de que adoptara oficialmente el nombre de Meta y se centró en las acusaciones de que la consultora política Cambridge Analytica había accedido indebidamente a los datos de 87 millones de usuarios, lo que suscitó dudas sobre las prácticas de Facebook en la gestión de la información personal.
sources.headline: Un juez condena a Meta a pagar 25.000 millones por vender datos de usuarios con fines electorales

stories.headline: Republicans' TV advertising advantage is diluted by reliance on outside groups

sources.body: Republicans are banking on a massive cash edge to help save their majority in Congress. But they are losing much of that advantage in an important arena: broadcast TV ads. Republicans have spent $677 million on those ads across 10 key Senate battleground states, compared to $479 million by the Democrats. But the GOP’s money isn’t going nearly as far because they’re more dependent on outside groups that pay much higher rates than candidates. The disparity has helped Democrats stay in the fight for Senate control amid an onslaught of GOP outside spending. In Ohio’s Senate race, Republican groups make up 63% of the $218 million spent. But in spite of their nearly 2-to-1 spending advantage over Democrats, they make up just over half of ads that are on the airwaves, according to data from the tracking service AdImpact. In Texas, Republicans have outspent Democrats by a 3-to-1 margin but have aired just 58% of the ads. And in Michigan, the GOP accounts for 60% of the spending but just over half of the ads. A large part of this discrepancy comes down to the mechanics of broadcast advertising. Candidates, and now political parties thanks to a recent Supreme Court ruling, are entitled to significantly lower rates. That has allowed Democratic candidates — who have posted bonkers fundraising hauls — to offset much of the GOP advantage in super PACs. Republican Senate candidates, on the other hand, struggled overall with their fundraising. And some GOP outside groups bought their ad time later, when it was even more expensive. “There are limitations to the impact of ‘big money’ in politics,” said Sean Cooksey, a Republican and former chair of the Federal Election Commission. “It's a good demonstration of the economics of campaign fundraising. Hard dollars really just go so much further.” The disparity also shows “the Republican overreliance on outside groups,” said Ian Russell, a Democratic admaker. “You get an eye-popping dollar amount, but it doesn't actually translate into as many spots as you would think relative to a well-financed candidate,” Russell said. “[Republicans] were just hoping that they could spend their way out of everything that was going wrong for them. But the problem is, their issues run much deeper than a few ad buys can fix. Especially when you've got monster fundraising hauls from the Democratic side.” Republicans in House and Senate races have long been more dependent on outside groups and megadonors, and for multiple cycles have seen their cash advantage undercut by fundraising strength from individual Democratic candidates. But that trend is particularly pronounced this year given the combination of Republican super PAC money and their candidates’ struggles. In 2024, Republican outside groups spent only about 15% more than Democrats on TV ads across House and Senate general election contests, according to a POLITICO analysis of AdImpact data. This cycle, GOP outside groups have spent 7% more. In a few states, the discrepancy between dollars and airtime is less stark. Republicans account for 60% of the spending in Maine’s Senate race and an equal percentage of the ads, according to AdImpact. That’s in part because Sen. Susan Collins has outraised her Democratic opponent Troy Jackson over the whole cycle, although Jackson, who didn’t launch his campaign until July, raised far more in the third quarter. The numbers show the shifting dynamics of campaign strategy after the Supreme Court opened the floodgates to more spending from parties by granting them the lower advertising rate. Republicans have been faster to take advantage of the new rules: Major coordinated spending efforts from the NRSC and RNC have helped their side significantly this cycle. Republicans have far outspent Democrats on Senate party-coordinated Senate advertising, $90 million to $34.6 million across TV, radio and digital ads, according to data from AdImpact. “If I were the leader of either party, I would say you shouldn't give a dollar, you shouldn't give a single penny to these super PACs until you've maxed out to the party committee,” Cooksey said. Some Republicans say that strategic errors have contributed to erasing their cash edge. A number of GOP strategists have also privately griped that MAGA Inc. — one of the major outside groups backing their candidates — bought TV airtime too late, forcing them to pay even higher rates and further draining resources and increasing the price of reaching voters. Republicans fretted for months about whether Trump’s well-financed super PAC, MAGA Inc., would get involved . The group has since spent heavily but only launched its first general election ad buys in September. “There is no question MAGA Inc. should have bought ads earlier in the cycle,” said one national GOP operative who was granted anonymity to discuss party strategy, noting that rates across the country increase as Election Day nears. Other top GOP outside groups, like the Senate Leadership Fund and the Congressional Leadership Fund, made their early advertising reservations much earlier in the cycle than MAGA Inc. Trump allies waved away that criticism. A person familiar with the Trump operation’s midterm planning, granted anonymity to discuss strategy, said it’s "indisputable that the spending from the Trump political effort has kept us competitive in many Senate races.” MAGA Inc. declined to comment. Still, GOP outside groups are utilizing their cash advantage in some underappreciated ways. Republican super PACs have massively outspent their Democratic counterparts on mail — roughly $157 million to $35 million for the general election — according to a POLITICO analysis of independent expenditure filings submitted to the Federal Election Commission. That’s led by a whopping $44 million in spending on mail across 24 races from the Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC, along with $23.8 million across 20 races from Elon Musk’s America PAC. GOP-aligned super PACs have also spent more than Democratic ones on phone calls and text messages, the data shows.
sources.headline: Why Republicans’ massive cash advantage is evaporating on the airwaves

stories.headline: Georgia Republicans look to Rick Jackson to contain a potential midterm wipeout

sources.body: Georgia Republicans are counting on Rick Jackson to save them from a wipeout in November — if President Donald Trump doesn’t get in the way. The billionaire health care executive and political newcomer has spent nearly $200 million since he entered the Georgia governor’s race earlier this year. That’s boosted GOP hopes as many in the party have all but given up on the state’s marquee Senate race, where Rep. Mike Collins is struggling to close the gap against a formidably well-funded Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff. Republicans worry that their open contests for attorney general and lieutenant governor as well as control of the state general assembly could be in peril in a larger blue wave. But Jackson’s deep pockets are being tested against a difficult political environment for Republicans, weighed down by unpopular Trump actions, including the war in Iran. And some in the GOP worry that the president’s repeated visits to Georgia could only make the situation worse. “I don't know that Trump coming helps Republicans more so than it excites Democrats, especially in a wave election year, and so becomes and becomes a catch-22 for Republican candidates,” said Jason Shepherd, a former Cobb County chair who is supporting Jackson. One Georgia-based Republican strategist who is not involved in the gubernatorial race posited that Trump’s dual appearances in the state almost certainly did more harm than help. They, like others in this article, were granted anonymity to speak openly about the race to avoid reprisals. “Every piece of data that I've seen, it is not MAGA Republicans that are unmotivated to vote in this election,” the person said. “All the data that I've seen is that the undecideds in our marquee races, and specifically in the governor's race, have a very, very negative opinion of the president. So, I can't really rationalize a case for how it would be helpful.” Jackson, for his part, has carefully navigated his relationship with the president and has not publicly broken with him on policy like other battleground Republicans. But he has not mentioned the president in any of the nearly 150 ads he’s run in the general election, according to an analysis of data from tracking firm AdImpact. Shortly after the RNC announced that Trump would return to the state this weekend, Jackson’s team said in a statement that the candidate will be campaigning in a different part of Georgia. And during his only televised gubernatorial debate on Oct. 6 against Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, Jackson never name-dropped the president — despite his opponent invoking Trump’s name eight times. Instead, the Republican mentioned popular outgoing GOP Gov. Brian Kemp five times and focused on Bottoms’ tenure as mayor of Atlanta during the Covid-19 pandemic. “It’s been proven time and again that when the message is on Georgia, and the results under Brian Kemp and the conservative vision and road map that's been laid out here, that we win in Georgia. When the focus is on D.C. and personal politics, we lose,” said Cole Muzio, president of the conservative Frontline Policy Action group .  The Jackson campaign declined to comment for this story. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that Republicans “are laser focused on winning, and our candidates will run the races necessary to best represent their districts and prevent Democrats from taking control." Jackson is one of several Republicans across the country who now must balance between keeping the president close enough to turn out Republican base voters, but not so closely as to alienate the center. Though many Georgia Republicans see Jackson as their de-facto ticket-topper, they don’t see his win as a guarantee against Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, in a finicky battleground state like Georgia. Jackson has outspent Bottoms nearly 5-to-1 in the final stretch of the race but still remains in a close race in public polling . And yet, without him, Republicans fear the bottom would have already fallen out on races up and down the ballot, given how poorly Collins is performing in polls against Ossoff. Republicans’ top Senate super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, was dark in Georgia last week , a sign the race may be slipping out of reach. “If Rick Jackson weren't running, we would all be in a lot of trouble,” said Stephen Lawson, a Georgia-based Republican strategist and Jackson ally. “He’s our best hope at keeping the state red.” A second Georgia-based Republican strategist, who is working on other races in the state, underscored how Jackson’s money is keeping the party afloat. “There is no question in my mind that without the extra $150 million he spent in his general election, that the ticket would be lost,” this person said. “That is the only reason there's still a fight to be had.” But, this person cautioned, the race is still very much a toss-up, and Jackson’s victory will rely on a large share of Georgia voters choosing to split their ballots between Ossoff for Senate and Jackson for governor. Jackson’s allies are optimistic that a significant number of voters will do just that. A private statewide poll reviewed by POLITICO found that roughly 19% of Georgia voters say they are definitely or likely to cast a vote for at least one Democrat and one Republican — a potentially significant pool of crossover voters that could power two very different results in the marquee contests. Whether the sheer force of Jackson’s spending will prove successful enough to overcome Trump is a microcosm of the larger issue his party is experiencing across the country: National Republicans, flush with cash, hold an enormous financial advantage over Democrats. But money alone may not be enough to insulate candidates in battlegrounds or even in traditionally red territory. “I don't know that Republicans across the country should feel as bullish about the cash influx that we've gotten because it didn't work here,” said the first GOP operative. “In terms of actively moving races in our favor, it at least didn't work here.” In the last month, as Bottoms began to spend more heavily on the air amid Jackson's spending advantage, her campaign has noted that polling has started to move marginally in her favor — even if the race remains largely within the margin of error . Her high name ID, as well as cash spent after the primary to define her early, are helping. “Rick Jackson has spent $200 million in this campaign but all the money in the world can’t hide the fact that he would be a lackey for Donald Trump,” TaNisha Cameron, a spokesperson for Bottoms, said in a statement. “Despite being outspent, Keisha’s message is breaking through and she has the momentum in this race right when it matters." Jackson is making more of an effort to tie himself closely to Kemp, who won over moderates and independents in his 2022 reelection for governor and has an approval rating that sits 30 points higher than the president’s in Georgia, according to a recent poll by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . Kemp, for his part, has continued to be a presence on the trail for Jackson, including joining him on a statewide tour earlier this month and appearing in at least three TV ads for the campaign. But Jackson’s pathway to victory requires him to not only secure crossover voters that may support Ossoff in the Senate race or the type of voters who broke for Kemp, but also turn out the MAGA base who powered the president’s two presidential victories in the perennial battleground. The president is intent on still showing up for him. Shortly after Jackson dispatched Trump’s initially preferred candidate, Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, in June’s primary runoff, the president was quick to praise Jackson as standing “strong with ‘TRUMP.’” And in subsequent posts on Truth Social, Trump has called the health care executive a “good friend.” Trump, onstage Friday, called Jackson a “great businessman,” before adding: “I’ve been watching you, you are good, and he never did this before. He did it because he wants to straighten out things and he’s an amazing, an amazing story.” Aaron Pellish contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Rick Jackson is the GOP’s best hope in Georgia right now

stories.headline: Brad Lander detained while joining West Bank olive harvest

sources.body: INTIFADA FLARE UP: One of New York City’s most prestigious public high schools is facing backlash because a school-based socialist youth group co-signed a social media post declaring “Intifada Until Victory!” The Young Democratic Socialists of America chapter of Stuyvesant High School — along with YDSA chapters at Hunter College, the New School, City College and Lehman College — all signed onto an Oct. 8 Instagram post that accused the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter of silencing student activists who wanted to protest Mayor Zohran Mamdani over Israel. The groups accused the democratic socialist mayor of betraying the Palestinian cause and blasted his decision to keep NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch in her position, referring to her as a “Zionist billionaire.” The term intifada — which refers to violent uprisings against Jews in Israel — is viewed by many Jews as a call to violence against them. Moshe Spern, president of United Jewish Teachers — an advocacy group representing Jewish teachers and students across the city — is demanding the posts be removed immediately and that the YDSA group provide a public apology to the school community. “NYC public schools have seen hundreds of antisemitic and anti-Israel incidents since October 7, 2023,” he wrote in an email yesterday to Stuyvesant Principal Seung Yu and New York City Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels. “When a school-recognized club amplifies this rhetoric, it risks contributing to a hostile environment.” In the missive, Spern invoked Title VI — the federal law that bans discrimination based on race, shared ancestry and national origin — and demanded a review of the YDSA chapter’s charter, faculty adviser and recent activities for compliance. Spern also cited a chancellor’s regulation that states that student clubs operate under the principal’s supervision and must remain consistent with the school’s educational goals. Yu did not respond to requests for comment. Mamdani’s Department of Education also did not respond to Playbook. Spern told Playbook today that he has yet to receive a response from Yu. “To flat out ignore it is extremely irresponsible,” he said. The NYC-DSA defended the organization. “We support the right to organize,” NYC-DSA co-Chair Gustavo Gordillo said in a statement. “NYC-DSA did not organize or endorse this particular rally, but red scare tactics have never been effective tools for engaging with student movements.” The social media uproar is the latest flashpoint in ongoing tensions in the city over Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the war that followed. Mamdani, a longtime critic of Israel, was reluctant to condemn the term “globalize the intifada” on the campaign trail last year before finally saying he will not use the term . He also drew bipartisan backlash over his statement marking the third anniversary of the attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu labeled the mayor an antisemite , which Mamdani has denied. Mamdani, though, has also simultaneously faced backlash from pro-Palestinian activists who accused him of betraying the Palestinian cause by retaining Tisch, who’s Jewish and a self-described Zionist. Those critics have also criticized him for not doing enough to prevent local synagogues from holding events that promote land sales in Israel, some of them in the occupied West Bank. — Madina Touré From the Capitol Q’S LATEST: Gov. Kathy Hochul has a 55-41 lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, a Quinnipiac University poll released this afternoon found. That 14-point advantage is narrower than the 19-point lead Quinnipiac gave Hochul last month. But it’s more in line with the numbers from other pollsters: Marist found Hochul up by 11 two weeks ago, Emerson had Hochul up 12 in early October, and Siena measured her lead at 9 points last month. Despite Hochul’s lead, the Q Poll concluded Blakeman has an enthusiasm advantage. A total of 65% of his backers were “very enthusiastic” to support him, while only 33% of Hochul’s supporters said the same. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL LANDER DETAINED: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained today by Israeli security officials while harvesting olives in the West Bank. Lander, a self-described liberal Zionist and critic of Israel , said he went to the West Bank as part of the “Protect the Harvest” coalition to support Palestinians gathering crops. Rabbi Jill Jacobs, CEO of T’ruah, a progressive rabbinical organization, said she was also detained Wednesday, along with “approximately 80 American, Israeli, and international volunteers providing a protective presence for Palestinian farmers.” According to a press release from T’ruah, there were “approximately two hours of peaceful harvesting” until “Israeli forces declared the area a closed military zone” and detained them to transport them to a police station, despite the volunteers agreeing to leave. An Israeli military official told POLITICO that officers from the Israel Defense Forces and Border Police, along with local police, arrived at the scene because Palestinians did not submit a request to coordinate harvesting in that area, which is required ahead of time. The official added that the farm in question “requires only a small number of harvesters to collect its produce” and “the security establishment views the arrival of dozens of activists as an act intended solely to provoke, which undermines the harvesting process.” Lander was released “once the matter was brought to our attention” that he is a congressional candidate, the official said. Lander confirmed in a social media post that he was released with a “warning” because of his “public profile.” Read more from Madison Fernandez in POLITICO . IN OTHER NEWS — MUSK: Elon Musk has spent more than $500,000 to support Rep. Mike Lawler’s reelection bid against Democratic challenger Cait Conley. ( Gothamist ) — STOP: New York City deployed 600 red light cameras to intersections, the maximum number allowed under state law. ( New York Daily News ) — MEASLES: In the wake of a measles crisis, the state Health Department remains locked in a court battle with Amish schools over religious vaccine exemptions. ( The New York Times ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. Read it here .
sources.headline: NYC high school faces backlash over ‘intifada’ post

sources.body:
About 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers held near Nahalin in West Bank and taken to police station

The Israeli military has detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general.

“I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis and volunteers,” Lander posted from a bus taking him to a police station. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nahalin in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know.”

Lander, who is Jewish and an outspoken critic of the Israeli government, describes himself as a liberal Zionist. He believes in the vision of Israel as a safe, Jewish home, but argues that it cannot be a true democracy while it denies Palestinians their human rights and freedom.

An ally of the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, Lander’s critical approach to Israel was a key factor in his resounding primary victory against Dan Goldman, a prominent supporter of Israel.

He condemns Israel’s continued occupation of the West Bank and Gaza, supported the restriction of US military aid to Israel and believes that Israel’s military campaign in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks amounts to genocide.

Settler militants have unleashed extreme violence on Palestinians attempting to harvest olives from their trees across the occupied West Bank, and anyone accompanying them.

A vicious assault on a US photojournalist and attacks on European diplomats and a French mayor over the weekend drew international condemnation and calls for the Israeli government to crack down on militants.

Wednesday’s olive-picking from trees outside the village of Nahalin was uneventful until a large contingent of Israeli security forces arrived, the organisers Protect the Harvest said in a statement.

“All volunteers were peacefully harvesting on the private land of a Palestinian family who had invited them. For reasons that remain unclear, the Israeli army showed up and detained approximately 80 people who were present.”

Soldiers said the area had been declared a closed military zone, separated the group by nationality and drove them to a nearby police station in minibuses for the Israelis and a larger bus for Americans.

Joshua Schoffman, who served as Israel’s deputy attorney general for more than a decade, described the mass detention as a “complete hallucination” in a post on social media .

“Just now, they told me that I’m being detained for the crime of olive harvesting,” he wrote. “We were asked to stop, and everyone complied. There was no friction whatsoever with settlers or with the security forces.”

stories.headline: Constitutional Court leaves 160,000 naturalized Spaniards' voting rights unresolved

sources.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/JHGSSLEIYVB5PEQEM6UHNRP2CA.jpg?auth=30e70d2e5c0d5a5e154647bb627618542a07ec94336e5c5d68e86fcf73252e69" width="7162" height="4776" alt="Cándido Conde-Pumpido, presidente del Tribunal Constitucional, en la sede, en Madrid, el pasado 9 de octubre. "></img><p>El voto de 160.000 españoles en las próximas elecciones generales sigue en el aire; y, en concreto, en el tejado del Tribunal Supremo que había ratificado su suspensión el 12 de octubre pasado y a donde lo ha devuelto este miércoles el Tribunal Constitucional al rechazar de plano el recurso de amparo del Defensor del Pueblo contra esa suspensión cautelar del sufragio. El pleno del tribunal de garantías, por diez votos a dos, ha inadmitido <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-16/el-defensor-del-pueblo-interpone-un-recurso-de-amparo-ante-el-constitucional-por-la-suspension-del-derecho-al-voto-a-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-16/el-defensor-del-pueblo-interpone-un-recurso-de-amparo-ante-el-constitucional-por-la-suspension-del-derecho-al-voto-a-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html">el recurso del Defensor del Pueblo</a> que pedía restablecer el derecho al voto de los <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-20/los-consulados-ven-casi-imposible-diferenciar-a-tiempo-que-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos-podran-votar-el-29-n.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-20/los-consulados-ven-casi-imposible-diferenciar-a-tiempo-que-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos-podran-votar-el-29-n.html">160.000 nacionalizados</a> a quienes el Tribunal Supremo se lo había retirado el día de la Hispanidad. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/el-constitucional-rechaza-el-amparo-por-la-ley-de-nietos-con-el-voto-en-contra-de-dos-magistrados-progresistas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El Constitucional rechaza el amparo por la ‘ley de nietos’ y deja en el aire el voto de 160.000 españoles

sources.body:
Cándido Conde-Pumpido, presidente del Tribunal Constitucional

Algo más de 160.000 descendientes de exiliados del franquismo y nacionalizados españoles no podrán ejercer su derecho al voto en las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. El Defensor del Pueblo, Ángel Gabilondo, había tratado de abrir la puerta para concederles el sufragio, pero ayer el Tribunal Constitucional la cerró.

El pleno del Constitucional decidió por diez votos a favor, incluido el de su presidente, Cándido Conde-Pumpido, no admitir a trámite un recurso de amparo interpuesto por Gabilondo contra una resolución del Tribunal Supremo que suspende de momento el derecho al voto de estos exiliados. Dos magistrados del Constitucional, Ramón Sáez y Juan Carlos Campo, se opusieron a la decisión mayoritaria y anunciaron que formularán votos particulares.

La decisión de esos diez magistrados se fundamenta en el hecho de que la resolución del Supremo impugnada por Gabilondo no es definitiva. El Constitucional solo puede tomar cartas en un asunto cuando este ya está totalmente sustanciado en la anterior instancia, es decir, cuando ya hay sentencia firme. Como ese no es el caso, el Constitucional no admitió al recurso del Defensor del Pueblo a trámite al considerarlo “prematuro”.

Esta decisión es tan solo un paso más a un complejo proceso judicial que se inició con la llamada  ley de nietos  . En el año 2022 se aprobó la ley de Memoria Democrática, cuya disposición adicional octava establece que pueden optar a la nacionalidad española “los nacidos fuera de España de padre o madre, abuelo o abuela, que originariamente hubieran sido españoles y que, como consecuencia de haber sufrido exilio por razones políticas, ideológicas o de creencia o de orientación e identidad sexual, hubieran perdido o renunciado a la nacionalidad española”.

Poco después, ese mismo año, el Gobierno dictó una instrucción para determinar cómo debían realizarse esos procesos de nacionalización. La instrucción, a criterio de los denunciantes, iba más allá de la norma al establecer que “se presumirá la condición de exiliado respecto de todos los españoles que salieron de España entre el 18 de julio de 1936 y el 31 de diciembre de 1955. En estos supuestos, solo deberá acreditarse la salida del territorio español. Si la salida de España se produjo entre el 1 de enero de 1956 y el 28 de diciembre de 1978, deberá acreditarse la condición de e­xiliado”.

Los partidos Iustitia Europa y Vox recurrieron esa instrucción ante el Supremo al considerar que es nula de pleno derecho. También pidieron que dejara de aplicarse hasta que el Alto Tribunal resuelva sobre el fondo de la cuestión. El 12 de octubre, el Supremo dictó una resolución por la que no pone pegas a que voten el 29 de noviembre las personas que han adquirido la na­cionalidad­ española de acuerdo con la ley­ de Memoria Democrática, pero sí suspende el derecho a voto de los nacionalizados a través de la instrucción, unas 163.000 per­sonas.

Esa es la decisión que Gabilondo llevó al Tribunal Constitucional. La reclamación no ha tenido éxito. Tanto el Defensor del Pueblo como el Gobierno han manifestado su “respeto” por la resolución del Constitucional, al tiempo que han mostrado su “preocupación” por el hecho de que haya ciudadanos que pierdan el derecho al sufragio. Además, el Ejecutivo ha expresado la dificultad que acarrea excluir del censo a esos  nietos  a estas alturas de la carrera electoral.
sources.headline: El voto de los nacionalizados queda en manos del Supremo en tiempo de descuento

stories.headline: Javier Milei's Madrid visit becomes a flashpoint in Spain's election campaign

sources.body: <p>Cuando se confirmó que Javier Milei volvía a España pero esta vez en plena precampaña electoral, el equipo de campaña del presidente del Gobierno, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-participa-en-un-desayuno-informativo-en-madrid-durante-su-visita-a-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-21/milei-participa-en-un-desayuno-informativo-en-madrid-durante-su-visita-a-espana.html">Pedro Sánchez,</a> no daba crédito. Parecía un regalo perfecto. Y lo fue. Hasta el alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, del PP, admitió que el viaje era un caramelo para el presidente. “Pedro Sánchez será el primero que esté muy feliz por la propaganda que le ha dado Milei hoy, estoy seguro”, llegó a decir el regidor.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/milei-agita-la-campana-con-insultos-a-sanchez-y-abrazos-a-ayuso.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Milei agita la campaña con insultos a Sánchez y abrazos a Ayuso

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno y líder del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez , ha asegurado este miércoles que el presidente de Argentina , Javier Milei , es "la misma peña" que Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal , la de "los recortes, los tijeretazos y la motosierra".

Durante un acto de precampaña electoral organizado por el PSOE en el Fórum Evolución de Burgos, Sánchez ha augurado que el 29 de noviembre los votantes van a enviar a los dirigentes del PP y Vox "al aserradero", porque los tienen "muy calados" y representan para España lo mismo que Milei para Argentina.

Según Sánchez, "el presidente de Argentina ha venido aquí y les ha creado un problema". " Feijóo y Abascal le invitaron y ahora no saben qué hacer con él, porque como les han dicho que no hablen de recortes hasta el 29N, ahora no saben de qué hablar", ha expresado Sánchez, que por segunda vez en tres días tiene un mitin en Castilla y León. "Y ahí está Feijóo, hablando de pizzas y pisos y Abascal diciendo 'uy me habéis pillado fuera, hacemos zoom porque estoy fuera de Madrid", se ha referido Sánchez reaccionando a las palabras de Feijóo de este miércoles, que ha asegurado que "hay propietarios con miedo porque si un okupa llega con un papel de haber pedido una pizza, ya nadie le puede sacar hasta dentro de varios años".

"A quien pretendéis engañar, Alberto y Santiago, si os tenemos muy calados , si formáis todos las misma peña, Milei, Feijóo y Abascal: la de los recortes, tijeretazo y motosierra. El próximo 29N os vamos a llevar al aserradero y seguir gobernando cuatro años más", ha dicho Sánchez en Burgos.

El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE el 29N ha hecho estas declaraciones horas después de que Milei le haya llamado "impresentable dictador ", al tiempo que ha hecho un llamamiento al "liberalismo" a "sacar a los socialistas a patadas". De hecho, aunque no se han encontrado presencialmente porque Abascal ha programado su agenda para estar fuera de Madrid, ambos han intercambiado una videollamada. En ella el argentino le ha asegurado al líder de la ultraderecha española que "no hay nada más divertido que patear culos zurdos".

Y mientras tanto, en el mitin en Burgos, Sánchez ha mostrado "mucho orgullo por ser zurdos y zurdas" . "Lo dicen como si fuera un insulto. Pues a mucha honra, con esta mano izquierda hemos subido las pensiones que ellos quieren recortar o subido el SMI que ellos quieren congelar. Esa es la causa de los zurdos", ha dicho el presidente del Gobierno entre aplausos de los asistentes.

"Las motosierras y tijeretazos que la derecha y ultraderecha hacen cuando gobiernan no unen ni cohesionan, dividen y fragmentan", ha avisado Sánchez. "No hacen que crezca nuestro país, de eso Milei podrá venir a dar lecciones, pero de todas nos queda una muy clara, que es que si sus amigos Feijóo y Abascal ganan, van a hacer con España lo que está haciendo Milei con Argentina", ha finalizado comparando los malos datos económicos argentinos con los de España.

stories.headline: More than 100 migrants who entered Ceuta in July receive asylum

sources.body: <p>En torno a un centenar de migrantes que entraron en Ceuta entre el 30 y el 31 de julio ya tienen la protección internacional que les permite permanecer legalmente en España y les reconoce el derecho a residir y trabajar en el país. Así lo han confirmado a este periódico diversas fuentes internas, que constatan que las resoluciones de asilo concedidas desde el 31 de julio ascienden a 180 expedientes. No obstante, no todas son de migrantes que llegaron a Ceuta <a href="" rel="" title="">en el cruce masivo</a>, sino que algunos de ellos corresponden a personas que ya estaban previamente en la ciudad. Los relativos a las personas que llegaron a finales de julio se cifran en algo más de un centenar. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-22/mas-de-100-migrantes-de-ceuta-han-recibido-el-asilo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/RCBFQVBGMZHKDNJ2ZQ5FX3G3G4.jpg?auth=ace9e48eca3d561630d3bc1cc145937ce088fc4fe429687edb812aa5d34612b5" width="4724" height="3151" alt="Tres jóvenes migrantes en el paseo de la playa de Benítez, en Ceuta."></img>

sources.body: <p>Este octubre se cumplen seis meses desde que el PP inaugurase la segunda ronda de Gobiernos autonómicos con Vox. María Guardiola, baronesa extremeña, cedía de nuevo ante la extrema derecha incluyéndola en su Ejecutivo y desataba la caída del resto de fichas del dominó: Aragón, Castilla y León y Andalucía. stories.headline: Barcelona prepares phased reopening of Collserola after swine-fever restrictions

sources.body: (ACN) L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ja està preparant una proposta per treballar sobre les zones de Collserola que es podrien començar a desescalar quan es reobri el parc natural a finals d’any, com va anunciar diumenge el conseller d’Agricultura, Òscar Ordeig . La intenció del consistori és fer-ho en funció del risc i mantenint els criteris de seguretat que es considerin oportuns per la crisi de la pesta porcina . Sobre la desescalada, una de les zones que l’Ajuntament vol reclamar que s’obri és la carretera de les Aigües , segons ha dit el tinent d’alcaldia de Seguretat, Albert Batlle , a la Comissió d’Ecologia, Urbanisme, Mobilitat i Habitatge. “Des de l’Ajuntament ja estem preparant una proposta per elevar-la a la conselleria”, ha dit Batlle. El Parc de Collserola està tancat des de fa set mesos , quan es va detectar el primer cas d’un senglar infectat per la pesta porcina a la ciutat. També et pot interessar El govern preveu reobrir Collserola a finals d’any “amb corredors segurs” Núria Granados 1 minut de lectura Batlle recorda que cal ser prudents Batlle s’ha remès a les declaracions del mateix conseller Òscar Ordeig del cap de setmana i ha recordat que la Generalitat ha creat un grup tècnic i una taula de coordinació política per començar a treballar les zones de Collserola que es podrien desescalar de forma gradual. Tot i això, ha recordat que les decisions responen a condicions tècniques i científiques d’acord amb els protocols i amb la normativa europea. “Decisions que tots hem de respectar perquè ens hi juguem conseqüències econòmiques molt greus per al país, pèrdua de mercats internacionals, restriccions comercials i un impacte sever sobre el sector”, ha apuntat. Així, ha demanat mantenir la prudència tot i reconèixer que són molt conscients de les molèsties que suposen les restriccions de Collserola . També et pot interessar Veïns del Parc de Collserola reclamen que reobri per salut mental: “Alguns tenim ansietat” Jordi Escofet 2 minuts de lectura Celebració amb alguns “peròs” Veïns i comerciants de la zona han celebrat el comunicat, tot i que amb reserves per la repercussió que han tingut aquests mesos de tancament. Mentre el veïnat apunta que és una gran notícia per reprendre l’oci a la natura, els comerciants alerten que fa mesos que pateixen les conseqüències del tancament: “Ara podrem treballar novembre i desembre, però això no compensa els darrers 10 mesos”, apunta Sílvia Baldellou, de l’Associació de Comerciants de Vallvidrera. En aquest sentit, expliquen, acumulen moltes pèrdues i que els ingressos han baixat entre un 10 i un 15 %.

stories.headline: TMB bus strike called off after management and unions reach preliminary deal

sources.body:
Aquesta matinada s'ha desconvocat la vaga d'autobusos de Barcelona , que preveia aturades aquest dimecres, dijous i cinc dies més aquest octubre.

La direcció de la companyia i els sindicats han pactat un nou conveni col·lectiu, que tindrà una vigència de quatre anys .

El preacord garanteix més dies de descans i preveu una reducció progressiva de la jornada laboral fins a les 35 hores setmanals.

L'any que ve, els treballadors de bus tindran 10 dies més de descans. Podran sumar tres dies més si es donen determinades condicions com l'absentisme o millores operatives que permetin aconseguir prou estalvis per contractar més personal.

També han aconseguit més dies de descans en cap de setmana.

L'acord també ha permès desconvocar les cinc jornades de protestes més que s'havien programat per a aquest mes.

🚍 Desconvocada la vaga de #busbcn de TMB 👉 La direcció de TMB i el comitè de vaga han arribat a un acord que ha portat els sindicats a desconvocar les aturades previstes avui dimecres i altres 5 dies del mes d'octubre ➕Info: https://t.co/OSILu3RTUM https://t.co/SQ0RiNgHvh

La plantilla d'autobusos de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) estava convocada aquesta setmana a dues noves jornades de vagues parcials. La primera era aquest dimecres 14 i la intenció era repetir-la aquest dijous 15 d'octubre.

El Departament d'Empresa i Treball havia establert uns serveis mínims que oscil·laven entre el 40 i el 20%. Durant la resta de la jornada, es preveia que el servei fos l'habitual.

Les vagues parcials d'aquesta setmana formaven part de les set que el comitè d'empresa va anunciar per a aquest octubre després que al setembre no s'assolís cap acord entre l'empresa i els sindicats davant la demanda de millores laborals i salarials.

La primera va ser la setmana passada. Abans del preacord també n'hi havia de previstes per als dies 20, 22, 27 i 29 d'octubre.

Els treballadors del servei d'autobusos reclamaven millores en els calendaris laborals i la reducció de la jornada a 35 hores setmanals. Volien, a més, que s'apliquessin des del 2027 i no de manera diferida, com plantejava la direcció.

A més de canvis en el conveni com l' augment salarial , la millora de calendaris per a tots els col·lectius o el lot de Nadal , també denunciaven que no se'ls apliquen els dos dies de descans consecutius a la setmana que els pertoquen per llei.

Tant aquests descansos setmanals com la reducció de la jornada són les línies vermelles que la plantilla marcava en la negociació, segons el comitè d'empresa.
sources.headline: Desconvocada la vaga d'autobusos de TMB: direcció i sindicats tanquen un preacord de matinada

stories.headline: Barcelona weighs collaborative purchase to preserve homes in the Bloc Papallona

sources.body: L’habitatge ha tornat a centrar bona part del discurs del síndic de greuges de Barcelona, David Bondia, que ha advertit a l’ Infobarris que ha proposat una compra col·laborativa del Bloc Papallona , a la Nova Esquerra de l’Eixample. El síndic que ha mediat entre el veïnat, les entitats socials, la propietat i l’Ajuntament ha assegurat que hi ha diverses propostes sobre la taula , com ara la compra dels immobles per part d’entitats vinculades a l’habitatge o la seva incorporació a la borsa de lloguer social. Ha estat contundent en proposar una actuació d’urgència: “ Fer taxacions dels blocs i veure què pot passar, si pot ser una compra col·laborativa, si poden entitats del sector de l’habitatge comprar aquests blocs i si poden entrar a la borsa de lloguer social”. La proposta arriba després que el tinent d’alcaldia d’Economia, Hisenda, Promoció Econòmica i Turisme, Jordi Valls, anunciés que “l’Ajuntament no ho ha de comprar tot” i que cal explorar altres fórmules que permetin als veïns continuar vivint als seus habitatges. També et pot interessar Vaga de lloguers al Bloc Papallona: els veïns reclamen la renovació dels contractes Francis Manzano Rojas Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura “Sense habitatges no hi ha drets socials” Segons Bondia, la pressió dels moviments socials ha contribuït a fer replantejar algunes pràctiques dels fons d’inversió i ha reclamat mantenir obertes les vies de diàleg per evitar l’expulsió de veïns dels barris: “La ciutat necessita un canvi de model perquè garantir l’accés a un habitatge digne és la base de molts altres drets. Sense habitatge no hi drets socials” . El síndic, que acaba de renovar el càrrec , ha defensat més inversió en habitatge públic, una millor gestió del parc municipal i l’acceleració de la rehabilitació d’edificis amb problemes estructurals en barris com el Besòs, el Maresme i la Trinitat Vella. A més, Bondia ha destacat la necessitat de recuperar pisos buits per a ús residencial i social , una realitat que, segons ha constatat en les seves visites als barris, és especialment visible a Gràcia on un equip de betevé ha estat testimoni de la trobada. A Collserola “les restriccions han de ser l’excepció” També s’ha referit a la crisi de la pesta porcina i el tancament de Collserola. El síndic ha sentenciat que les ajudes econòmiques per establiments que acreditin pèrdues superiors al 30 % “ arriben molt tard i s’haurien d’haver previst abans “. No es cobraran fins al febrer del 2027 perquè hauran de tancar el comptes d’aquest any per comptabilitzar les pèrdues i, mentrestant, Bondia ha subratllat que molts hauran de fer acomiadaments. De fet, pel camí han tancat comerços. El síndic ha demanat que es creïn itineraris segurs, perquè “ la limitació (de circulació) no sigui la regla, sinó sigui l’excepció “. Ha apostat per prohibir només l’accés en zones on estigui acreditat que hi ha el virus, “però reobrir camins en zones epidemiològiques segures. S’ha de prevenir, però també el que podem fer és limitar la zona de restricció”, ha considerat Bondia, i ha lamentat que estem massa acostumats a mesures de caràcter general. Reclama que s’acotin on estigui el brot. Unes declaracions que arriben després que l’Ajuntament ha anunciat la reobertura esglaonada de Collserola i prioritza la carretera de les Aigües. El síndic a l’ Infobarris

stories.headline: Barcelona retailers and city hall clash over proposed commercial-rent regulation

sources.body: La XI edició del Summit Barcelona Oberta ha servit per posar blanc sobre negre als acords i desacords que aquesta entitat —que agrupa 24 eixos comercials— manté amb les polítiques de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona en alguns camps. Els lloguers comercials en són un exemple. L’alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni , ha anat al gra a l’hora de posar el tema sobre la taula: “Cal obrir el debat sobre la regulació dels lloguers comercials , especialment en la successió de contractes amb algunes pujades que han expulsat el comerç tradicional del barri “, ha dit en la primera intervenció de l’acte. I poc després Barcelona Oberta ha reiterat que no hi estan d’acord. Ben al contrari, ho emmarquen en el que qualifiquen d’excés d’intervencionisme de les administracions, i ho equiparen a la xarxa de supermercats públics , que també rebutgen. L’XI Summit de Barcelona Oberta ha portat per nom ‘La Barcelona que podria ser’ i ha servit a l’entitat per reclamar a les administracions “que facilitin l’activitat econòmica i es deixi de posar traves al comerç”. En aquest sentit, demanen millorar l’accessibilitat, flexibilitzar els plans d’usos, més agilitat administrativa i poder obrir els diumenges , una reivindicació històrica de l’entitat. També diferents eixos comercials hi han expressat les seves inquietuds i peticions. Crit d’auxili de Ciutat Vella Especialment preocupats s’han mostrat des de Barnacentre , que lamenten la pèrdua de diversitat comercial a Ciutat Vella . “Hem perdut la gran majoria del nostre comerç. Com el portarem una altra vegada?”, ha exclamat Núria Raja. I ha llançat un dard també per la mobilitat: “El tema de la mobilitat el tenim molt espatllat, i a Ciutat Vella no ens arriben els clients, els amics i la gent que necessitem. Hi ha molt turista, però volem la gent de casa”, ha etzibat. Teresa Guirado de Diagonal Boulevard ha expressat el temor per quan arribin les obres de la connexió del tramvia fins a Francesc Macià . “Necessitem informació, previsió i interlocució sobre una infraestructura com aquesta”. I per això, reclamen conèixer el projecte amb antelació, el calendari i les afectacions als accessos. Proposen, de fet, crear una taula i ser-hi presents per poder estar al cas de tot i dir-hi la seva. Des de Gaudí Shopping celebren que es posi fil a l’agulla a la reforma de l’avinguda de Gaudí. L’ Eix Pelai espera que es faci realitat la rehabilitació que ha de convertir el carrer en un bulevard . I des d’ Amics de la Rambla , Fermín Villar ha recordat que “la Rambla recull i genera molta taxa turística i seria de justícia que se li retorni”. També han expressat les seves inquietuds altres entitats com Som Sant Antoni , Born Comerç i els comerciants de la plaça Reial . “Comprar és com votar” A la trobada tothom ha estat d’acord que el comerç local forma part de la identitat de la ciutat. I que no només es tracta de negocis que generen llocs de treball i ingressos fiscals, sinó també d’una xarxa que proporciona cohesió, seguretat i dinamització als barris. És prioritari, coincideix tothom, preservar-ho, però “per moltes polítiques públiques que fem, si la gent no va a comprar a la botiga del barri això no val”, ha recordat Collboni. “Comprar és com votar”, ha dit l’alcalde, “perquè decidir on comprar és decidir quina ciutat estem fent. Si compro aquí o allà, estic determinant quin tipus d’economia i comerç tindré al meu barri”. Pel que fa a Barcelona Oberta, el president, Gabriel Jené, ha expressat la voluntat del sector de participar en les solucions i ha demanat convertir les reflexions del Summit en decisions, acords i millores visibles als carrers.
sources.headline: Barcelona Oberta demana deixar de posar traves al comerç i facilitar l’activitat econòmica
